title_en: Shanghai Municipal People's Procuratorate, Second Branch v. Wang Yibing — embezzlement case
keywords_en: criminal; embezzlement; first instance; intermediate people's court; Shanghai; natural person; criminal law; determination of subject of embezzlement crime; determination of embezzlement intent; determination of illegal possession of public funds; support for public prosecution; enterprise restructuring; transfer of public property; false accounting
full_text_en:
Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Procuratorate v. Wang Yibing — Embezzlement Case

[Ruling Summary]

In the process of enterprise restructuring, where an employee of a state-owned enterprise takes advantage of his or her position of being delegated to engage in public service in a state-collective joint venture, and transfers public property of the state-collective joint venture to a personal joint-stock company controlled by the employee and his or her relatives for illegal possession, such conduct shall be determined to constitute the crime of embezzlement.

Prosecutor: Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Procuratorate.

Defendant: Wang Yibing, male, 55 years old, legal representative and general manager of Shanghai Baoyao Building Materials Industrial Engineering Company, legal representative and chairman of the board of Shanghai Baoyao Building Materials Industrial Design and Research Institute. Arrested on August 17, 2001.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Procuratorate initiated a public prosecution against the defendant Wang Yibing for the crime of embezzlement, submitting the case to the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court.

The indictment alleged: During the period from 1994 to 1997, the defendant Wang Yibing, taking advantage of his position as general manager of Shanghai Baoyao Building Materials Industrial Engineering Company (hereinafter referred to as Baoyao Company), repeatedly instructed the company's financial personnel to conceal the truth, alter financial accounts, and take other measures to transfer the enterprise's property to Shanghai Baoyao Building Materials Industrial Design and Research Institute (hereinafter referred to as Baoyao Research Institute), in which he and his relatives held shares, and to concrete mixing stations operated by individual investors including his relatives, which were affiliated with Baoyao Company. These funds were used to purchase equipment or for investment, amounting to a total misappropriation of public funds of RMB 11,747,116.10. This constituted the crime of embezzlement and should be punished according to law.

The defendant Wang Yibing denied committing the crime of embezzlement.

The defense counsel for the defendant Wang Yibing argued that Wang Yibing did not meet the subject requirements for the crime of embezzlement, lacked the intent to commit embezzlement, and did not take public funds for his own possession, and therefore did not constitute the crime of embezzlement.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court found through trial:

Baoyao Company was a state-collectively owned joint venture enterprise jointly invested and established in July 1992 by Shanghai No. 13 Metallurgical Construction Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Metallurgical Company) and Shanghai Yaohua Cement Plant (hereinafter referred to as Yaohua Cement Plant). The defendant Wang Yibing was delegated by Metallurgical Company to serve as the legal representative and general manager of the company.

In June 1993, upon the proposal of the defendant Wang Yibing, Baoyao Company invested and established the Baoyao Research Institute, a collectively owned enterprise, with Wang Yibing responsible for its operation. By 1997, Baoyao Research Institute had been restructured into a joint-stock cooperative enterprise with all capital contributed by individual employees. Among the contributors, Wang Yibing's relatives, including his wife, mother, daughter, brother, and sister, invested a total of RMB 1.04 million, accounting for 69% of the total capital. Wang Yibing served as the legal representative, chairman of the board, and was responsible for its operation.

At the end of 1994, the defendant Wang Yibing instructed the chief financial officer, Song Zongyong, to take advantage of his concurrent position as an accountant at Baoyao Research Institute. By extracting financial vouchers from Baoyao Company and falsely recording them in the accounts of Baoyao Research Institute, and by altering the accounts of Baoyao Company, Wang Yibing transferred the profits of Baoyao Company to the accounts of Baoyao Research Institute, or used them to offset fees payable by Baoyao Research Institute to Baoyao Company. Specifically:

(1) During 1994, Baoyao Company received concrete payments totaling RMB 8,023,070 from Shanghai No. 5 Metallurgical Construction Co., Ltd., Shanghai No. 7 Construction Engineering Company, Shanghai Pudong Shangnan Real Estate Industrial Company, Shanghai International Construction Co., Ltd., and Shanghai No. 8 Construction Engineering Company, respectively. Wang Yibing instructed Song Zongyong, after issuing Baoyao Company's sales invoices, to use methods of creating false accounts. The bank deposit slips and Baoyao Company's sales invoices for this amount were recorded as receipt vouchers in the accounts of Baoyao Research Institute and used for Baoyao Research Institute's purchase of imported mixer trucks and other expenditures, totaling RMB 6,940,470. The relevant vouchers were all recorded in the management expense account and fixed asset account of Baoyao Research Institute. Additionally, in accordance with Wang Yibing's intention, Song Zongyong altered Baoyao Company's financial accounts, concealing and reducing Baoyao Company's receivables by a total of RMB 7,986,797.23.

(2) In March 1994, Baoyao Company issued checks of RMB 1.6 million and RMB 400,000, respectively, to Baoyao Research Institute. Baoyao Research Institute mainly used this money to purchase two Mitsubishi mixer trucks (Japanese) and recorded them as fixed assets. At the end of 1994, although Baoyao Research Institute had not actually repaid the loan, Song Zongyong falsified the accounts to create the illusion that Baoyao Research Institute had repaid Baoyao Company, resulting in Baoyao Company overpaying Baoyao Research Institute by RMB 1,991,323.59.

It was further found: In March 1995, Wang Yibing concealed the 1994 operating profits and the true circumstances of the vehicle purchases for Baoyao Research Institute at the Baoyao Company board of directors meeting, falsely reporting operating profits of only approximately RMB 4.238 million. Subsequently, because Wang Yibing had not turned over any profits, in October of the same year, the board of directors entered into a "Contract for Fixed Quota Profit Turnover Enterprise Contracted Operation" with Wang Yibing. The contract stipulated that during the contract period from the end of 1993 to the end of 1997, Wang Yibing must turn over a total profit of RMB 8.5 million, with RMB 4 million to be turned over for 1994 and RMB 1.5 million for each subsequent year. The balance of the profits after the turnover would be at Wang Yibing's disposal. However, up to the time of the incident, Wang Yibing had not turned over any profits.

It was also found: In June 1994, Lu Shusen, Jiang Shoucheng, Ying Jianshe, and others and their relatives invested RMB 1.5 million, and the defendant Wang Yibing invested RMB 500,000 in the names of his wife and brother, to jointly establish the "Pu-Yue Concrete Products Investment Consortium" (hereinafter referred to as "Pu-Yue Consortium"), which operated jointly with Baoyao Company in the form of Baoyao Company's No. 2 Mixing Station. This mixing station was not an independent legal entity; it was managed uniformly by Baoyao Company and subject to unified taxation, but it operated independently, maintained independent accounting, and was responsible for its own profits and losses. In 1996, it was contracted out to the Materials Department of Metallurgical Company. At the beginning of 1997, during settlement between the original shareholders, including Lu Shusen, and Baoyao Company, it was confirmed that the profits and depreciation of the mixing station from October 1994 to the end of 1995 totaled RMB 3.1 million. After deducting an advanced amount of RMB 2 million, the remaining profit was RMB 1.1 million. The settlement document was signed by Wang Yibing on behalf of Baoyao Company and by Lu Shusen on behalf of the Pu-Yue Consortium. It was also confirmed that all existing assets and equipment of the mixing station were appraised at RMB 1 million and transferred. Subsequently, Lu Shusen and others received the remaining profit and the equipment transfer fee totaling RMB 1,575,000 based on their shareholdings. In May 1997, Wang Yibing produced another settlement document confirming the operating balance of the mixing station as RMB 4,230,581.64 and instructed Song Zongyong to record it in Baoyao Company's financial accounts. This settlement document changed the settlement period to 1994 to 1996, increased income by over RMB 2 million, and carried forward input tax of over RMB 1.13 million. Song Zongyong used methods of creating false accounts, causing Baoyao Company to overpay the mixing station by over RMB 3.13 million. Lu Shusen and others did not sign to confirm this settlement document and did not receive any money. The main use of this portion of the money was as follows: RMB 750,000 was used to purchase equipment for the No. 2 Mixing Station, and RMB 2 million was remitted to Gao Zhongmou for investment.

After the case was filed, the investigative authorities seized a total of 15 vehicles, including mixer trucks and pump trucks, from Baoyao Research Institute; one savings deposit slip from China Minsheng Bank with a balance of RMB 395,482.44; cash of RMB 361,161.46; and USD 62,575.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court held:

1. Regarding whether the defendant Wang Yibing had the subject status for the crime of embezzlement.

Baoyao Company was a joint venture enterprise jointly invested by the state-owned enterprise Metallurgical Company and the collectively owned enterprise Yaohua Cement Plant. According to the joint venture contract, Metallurgical Company delegated Wang Yibing as a director, general manager, and legal representative of Baoyao Company, specifically responsible for Baoyao Company's production and operation. This indicates that Wang Yibing was a person delegated by a state-owned enterprise to engage in public service in a non-state-owned enterprise, meeting the subject requirement for the crime of embezzlement. Although Wang Yibing's appointment as general manager of Baoyao Company was made by the company's board of directors in accordance with the company's articles of association, this was a procedural step taken pursuant to the agreement between the joint venture parties. It does not negate the fact that Wang Yibing was delegated by a state-owned company to a non-state-owned company to exercise management authority on behalf of the state investor. The defense counsel's argument that Wang Yibing did not have the subject status for the crime of embezzlement cannot be sustained.

2. Regarding whether the defendant Wang Yibing had the intent to embezzle public funds.

After learning that Baoyao Company's total profit for 1994 exceeded RMB 18.48 million, Wang Yibing immediately instructed the accounting personnel to redo the accounts, changing the profit to over RMB 4 million and transferring the remaining profit to Baoyao Research Institute. Although Wang Yibing did not personally falsify the accounts, he took advantage of his concurrent positions as legal representative of both Baoyao Company and Baoyao Research Institute and his authority to manage the operations of both entities. By instructing the accounting personnel to carry out the act of illegally taking possession of Baoyao Company's public funds, he caused Baoyao Company's public funds to be transferred to Baoyao Research Institute. This demonstrates that Wang Yibing had a clear intent to illegally take possession of public funds. The defense counsel's argument that Wang Yibing lacked embezzlement intent cannot be sustained.

3. Regarding whether the defendant Wang Yibing illegally took possession of Baoyao Company's public funds.

After Baoyao Research Institute was restructured into a joint-stock cooperative enterprise with all capital contributed by individuals, Wang Yibing, as its legal representative, instructed others to falsify accounts to transfer Baoyao Company's public funds to Baoyao Research Institute, causing Baoyao Company to completely lose ownership of these public funds. Since these public funds were now entirely owned by Baoyao Research Institute, which was funded by individuals, and were actually controlled and disposed of by Wang Yibing, it should be determined that Wang Yibing's embezzlement was already completed. Whether Wang Yibing personally and directly took possession of the public funds or how much illegal benefit he obtained does not affect the determination of his criminal conduct. The defense counsel's argument that Wang Yibing did not illegally take possession of public funds cannot be sustained.

4. Regarding the issue of the contract for contracted operation signed by the defendant Wang Yibing.

Wang Yibing concealed the actual profits of Baoyao Company for 1994 and the situation where public funds of Baoyao Company were used to purchase equipment for Baoyao Research Institute, reporting false profits to the Baoyao Company board of directors. The board of directors, unaware of the true circumstances, decided to enter into a contract for contracted operation with Wang Yibing, which specified the profit turnover standards and stipulated that Wang Yibing could dispose of the remaining profits of the company at his own discretion, provided that the operating profit targets were met. This contract for contracted operation was entered into on the basis of false facts, contrary to the true intent of the signing parties, and was not performed by Wang Yibing. Therefore, it should be deemed invalid. The defense counsel's argument that Wang Yibing was engaged in contracted operation and was entitled to use the remaining profits of Baoyao Company cannot be sustained.

5. Whether Wang Yibing's act of causing Baoyao Research Institute to illegally take possession of Baoyao Company's loan of over RMB 1.99 million constituted embezzlement.

After Baoyao Company lent RMB 2 million to Baoyao Research Institute, Wang Yibing, with the intent to embezzle public funds, directly instructed others to issue a check from Baoyao Research Institute to Baoyao Company for a substantially identical amount, but without actual payment. This was done to create a false appearance of balancing the accounts, with the purpose of exempting Baoyao Research Institute from repaying the loan to Baoyao Company, thereby illegally taking possession of over RMB 1.99 million of Baoyao Company's funds. The defense counsel's argument that the over RMB 1.99 million did not enter the account of Baoyao Research Institute and therefore could not be determined as Wang Yibing's embezzlement of the public funds cannot be sustained.

6. Whether the defendant Wang Yibing embezzled RMB 2.75 million in public funds through false settlements regarding the mixing station.

After Baoyao Company paid Lu Shusen and others RMB 1.1 million in operating profits based on the settlement with the shareholders of the former No. 2 Mixing Station, Wang Yibing used another settlement document to instruct the accounting personnel to record it in the accounts, causing Baoyao Company to overpay the No. 2 Mixing Station by over RMB 3.13 million. The defense counsel submitted testimony from Song Zongyong that, during the settlement with Lu Shusen and others, because the profits payable were indeed under-settled, a second settlement was later conducted, and submitted the financial vouchers and documents on which the second settlement was based. The defense counsel also submitted testimony from Lu Shusen that Wang Yibing had underpaid during the first settlement. However, the settlement document that Wang Yibing instructed the accounting personnel to record contained the following suspicious points: First, this settlement document was only acknowledged by Baoyao Company, without the participation and acknowledgment of shareholders such as Lu Shusen, so its authenticity was uncertain; second, the vouchers and documents related to the second settlement submitted by Song Zongyong were not his own records, and there was insufficient factual basis to accept them; third, it was an objective fact that Song Zongyong had indeed created false accounts in Baoyao Company's accounts, increasing the profits allocated to the No. 2 Mixing Station; fourth, the settlement period in the second settlement document was from October 1994 to the end of 1996, but the No. 2 Mixing Station was no longer operated by the original shareholders including Lu Shusen during 1996; fifth, according to the second settlement, the No. 2 Mixing Station should have had an additional tax deduction of RMB 1.13 million, but there were no corresponding records in the accounts of Baoyao Company or the No. 2 Mixing Station. In summary, the defense counsel's argument that the settlement document Wang Yibing instructed the accounting personnel to record reflected the operating situation of the mixing station at the time cannot be accepted. However, the prosecutor's allegation that Wang Yibing fraudulently increased the profit paid by Baoyao Company to the No. 2 Mixing Station was based on the judicial accounting verification report. The conclusion of the judicial accounting verification report was in turn based on the settlement document signed by Wang Yibing and Lu Shusen respectively and the testimony of Song Zongyong during the investigation stage. Since the original vouchers and documents of the No. 2 Mixing Station were not obtained during the verification, it was impossible to determine whether Wang Yibing had engaged in fraudulently increasing profits. Furthermore, the testimony of witnesses Song Zongyong and Lu Shusen had changed. The prosecutor also failed to provide sufficient evidence to rule out the claims of Song Zongyong and Lu Shusen that Baoyao Company had underpaid profits during the settlement with the original shareholders of the mixing station. Therefore, the evidence for this part of the criminal facts alleged by the prosecutor was insufficient.

7. Regarding the specific amount of the defendant Wang Yibing's embezzlement.

In May 1994, the Baoyao Company board of directors had decided that after Wang Yibing achieved a profit target of RMB 3.8 million, he would receive a bonus of RMB 100,000. For the portion exceeding the target, 30% would be at Wang Yibing's disposal to reward himself and other meritorious personnel. Although Wang Yibing concealed the actual operating situation and the criminal facts of embezzlement when reporting the 1994 profit to the board of directors, this does not negate the validity of the board's prior decision that Wang Yibing was entitled to dispose of the bonus funds after achieving the profit target. The public funds of Baoyao Company that Wang Yibing illegally transferred to Baoyao Research Institute included the bonus funds that he could have disposed of according to the board's decision. Therefore, the bonus amount of RMB 2,082,141 to which he was entitled should be deducted from the Baoyao Company profits that Wang Yibing embezzled.

Additionally, among the criminal facts alleged by the prosecutor that Wang Yibing embezzled over RMB 7 million from Baoyao Company, there was a sum of RMB 65,322.51 in cash that had been paid by the bank, but there was no evidence to prove that this sum had been illegally taken by Wang Yibing or used in the operation of Baoyao Research Institute. Therefore, this sum cannot be determined as Wang Yibing's embezzlement.

In conclusion, the defendant Wang Yibing, as a state functionary, took advantage of his position and instructed others to falsify accounts to embezzle public funds amounting to RMB 6,849,652.59, an especially huge amount. His conduct constituted the crime of embezzlement and should be punished according to law. Considering that Wang Yibing used the embezzled public funds mainly for the production and operation activities of Baoyao Research Institute, and that the vehicles purchased with the illicit funds and some of the funds have been recovered, a lighter punishment may be imposed at the court's discretion.

Accordingly, on March 26, 2003, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court adjudicated:

1. The defendant Wang Yibing is convicted of embezzlement and sentenced to fifteen years' imprisonment, with the additional punishment of forfeiture of personal property of RMB 200,000.
2. The illegal gains shall be recovered. The recovered funds and the 15 mixer trucks and other vehicles, after being appraised and converted into value, shall be returned to the victimized unit, Shanghai Baoyao Building Materials Industrial Engineering Company. The shortfall shall be continuously recovered.

4. Testimony of witness Song Zongyong, Baoyao Company financial ledgers, Baoyao Laboratory financial ledgers, bank statements, judicial accounting verification reports, and other evidence to confirm that Wang Yibing instructed Song Zongyong to alter Baoyao Company's original accounts, extract some original vouchers and enter them into Baoyao Laboratory's ledgers, and transfer profits of over RMB 6.94 million originally belonging to Baoyao Company to Baoyao Laboratory for the purchase of imported mixer trucks and other expenses.

5. Testimony of witness Song Zongyong, Baoyao Company financial ledgers, Baoyao Laboratory financial ledgers, bank statements, judicial accounting verification reports, and other evidence to confirm the fact that in March 1994, Baoyao Company lent RMB 2 million to Baoyao Laboratory for the purchase of mixer trucks, and Baoyao Laboratory failed to repay the amount.

6. The guilty plea of Appellant Wang Yibing during the investigation phase of the case.

The Shanghai High People's Court holds as follows:

1. Regarding the legality of the interrogations of Wang Yibing by the investigation authorities.

This case was initiated based on a report by another person. On August 3, 2001, when the Baoshan District People's Procuratorate summoned Wang Yibing, he confessed on the same day that, after learning at the end of 1994 that Baoyao Company had realized profits of RMB 18 million, he believed he had put considerable effort into the management and operations, and thus developed selfish motives, and instructed accountant Song Zongyong to transfer payments received by Baoyao Company from its clients to Baoyao Laboratory for the purchase of mixer trucks and other expenses. This guilty plea was corroborated by video recording. Upon reviewing the videotape, no evidence of inducement or deception by the interrogators was found; Wang Yibing's confession was natural and fluent. Accordingly, the interrogations conducted by the procuratorial authorities were lawful. Therefore, Wang Yibing's defense that his guilty plea was made under inducement and deception lacks factual basis.

2. Regarding whether Wang Yibing has the status of a state functionary.

Baoyao Company is a state-owned and collective joint venture enterprise invested by the state-owned enterprise Metallurgical Company and the collective enterprise Yaohua Cement Plant. Wang Yibing, as a state functionary engaged in public service in a state-owned enterprise, was dispatched to the non-state-owned enterprise Baoyao Company to engage in public service. Pursuant to the provisions of Article 93, Paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, which stipulates that persons dispatched by a state-owned company to a non-state-owned company to engage in public service shall be treated as state functionaries, Wang Yibing shall be treated as a state functionary.

3. Regarding the ownership of the funds transferred by Wang Yibing.

In May 1994, the board of directors of Baoyao Company resolved to implement an economic responsibility contracting system, setting the profit target for 1994 at RMB 3.8 million, with a bonus of RMB 100,000 for Wang Yibing for meeting the target, and a 30% commission on the portion exceeding the target as a bonus for Wang Yibing. However, Wang Yibing concealed the true business performance and falsely reported to the board of directors that the operating profit for 1994 was RMB 4.238 million. The board of directors, relying on Wang Yibing's report without conducting an audit, resolved to award Wang Yibing a bonus of RMB 230,000, and after repeatedly urging Wang Yibing to turn over the 1994 profits to no avail, signed an "Enterprise Contracting Operation Contract for Fixed Profit Turnover Responsibility" with Wang Yibing. This contracting operation contract was signed under circumstances where Wang Yibing had falsely reported the 1994 profits, harming the interests of Baoyao Company, and shall be deemed invalid. The opinions of Wang Yibing and his defense counsel that Wang Yibing had the right to use the remaining profits of Baoyao Company cannot be sustained.

In summary, during 1994, Baoyao Laboratory was still a wholly-owned subsidiary of Baoyao Company. Wang Yibing's transfer of Baoyao Company's property to Baoyao Laboratory without proper accounting could not yet be punished as the crime of embezzlement. However, after Baoyao Laboratory was restructured into a individual shareholding cooperative enterprise in 1997, Wang Yibing, taking advantage of his position as General Manager of Baoyao Company, concealed the company's ownership of the assets of 12 mixer trucks at Baoyao Laboratory, causing this portion of public property, which originally belonged to Baoyao Company, to be illegally possessed by Baoyao Laboratory, which was absolutely controlled by Wang Yibing and his relatives. This conduct shall be punished as the crime of embezzlement. The amount of embezzlement shall be the value of the 12 mixer trucks and their accessories purchased with the illegally transferred funds, totaling over RMB 7 million.

Since the amount of embezzlement determined at the second instance is greater than that determined in the original judgment, in light of the provisions of Article 190, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which states that "when a court of second instance tries an appeal filed by the defendant or his legal representative, defender, or close relative, the punishment of the defendant shall not be increased," no additional punishment shall be imposed on Appellant Wang Yibing. The original judgment found the basic facts of Wang Yibing's crime of embezzlement to be clear, the evidence to be conclusive, the application of the law to be correct, the sentence to be appropriate, and the trial procedures to be lawful. The original judgment, considering that Wang Yibing had used the embezzled public funds primarily for the production and operation activities of Baoyao Laboratory, in which he and his relatives were the main investors, and that the vehicles purchased with the illicit funds and some of the funds had been recovered, gave Wang Yibing a lighter punishment based on the circumstances, which is not improper.

Accordingly, the Shanghai High People's Court ruled on September 30, 2003:

Appeal dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

This ruling is final.
